# Josh & Jordan's Kitchen

> No-talking home cooking and scratch baking from Josh & Jordan's Kitchen. Josh cooks savory meals by feel with no measuring cups; Jordan runs the oven. Tight method cuts, minimally cut full-process sessions, kitchen tools, and recipes.

Josh & Jordan's Kitchen is published by Built by Josh Studio LLC (https://builtbyjoshstudio.com/llms.txt). Contact: support@builtbyjoshstudio.com.

## Kitchen tools

- [Cookware & Pan Guide | Free Kitchen Utility](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/tools/cookware-pan-guide/): Select the best cookware material and pan shape for any cooking task. Interactive advisor, material explorer, and care guidelines. Free, ad-free, local-first.
- [Cost Per Serving Calculator | Free Recipe Cost Calculator](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/tools/cost-per-serving-calculator/): Free cost per serving calculator. Enter what you used, the pack size, and the pack price to get total recipe cost and price per serving. No signup, no ads.
- [Bread & Dough Hydration Calculator | Pizza & Pasta, Free](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/tools/dough-hydration-calculator/): Bread hydration calculator for bread, pizza, and pasta dough. Enter your flour and get water, salt, and yeast by baker's percentage. Free, no ads, no signup.
- [Turkey & Meat Thawing Time Calculator | Fridge or Cold Water](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/tools/meat-thawing-planner/): How long to thaw a turkey, chicken, roast, or steaks: enter the weight and get safe fridge and cold-water thawing times from USDA guidance. Free, no ads.
- [Baking Pan Conversion Calculator | Swap Cake Pan Sizes, Free](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/tools/pan-swap-calculator/): Swap one baking pan for another: round, square, rectangular, muffin, or Bundt. Get the ingredient multiplier and a bake-time warning. Free and ad-free.
- [Perfect Roast Pull Temp Calculator | Carryover Cooking Math](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/tools/perfect-roast-pull-temp-calculator/): Calculate the exact temperature to pull your roast, steak, or turkey from the oven to account for carryover cooking. A free, ad-free culinary utility.
- [Recipe Nutrition Calculator | Calories & Macros Per Serving](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/tools/recipe-nutrition-calculator/): Paste a recipe's ingredients and get calories, protein, carbs, and fat per serving, plus an estimated Nutrition Facts label. Free, no ads, no signup.
- [Roast Cooking Timeline Calculator | Reverse Timeline, Free](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/tools/reverse-roasting-calculator/): Pork roast cooking time, worked backward from dinner — enter a pork loin, shoulder, ham, turkey, or beef roast and serve time for an exact oven timeline. Free.
- [Universal Recipe Scaler | Ad-Free Ingredient Converter](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/tools/universal-recipe-scaler/): Instantly scale, multiply, or divide cooking and baking recipes. A free, local-first utility to convert portions and metric measurements with zero ads.

## Blog posts

- [The Baking Pan Swap Calculator — Free Pan Conversion Tool](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/baking-pan-swap-calculator/): Convert any recipe between pan sizes — square, round, rectangle, muffin tin, Bundt — with an instant scaling multiplier and bake-time warning. Free, no signup.
  - The short version: When a bake goes sideways between pan sizes, the recipe is rarely the problem — the pan geometry is. This is a free, ad-free, local-first utility: pick the pan a recipe calls for, pick the pan you actually own, and get the exact ingredient multiplier in one click. It covers cake-to-muffin-tin and Bundt conversions without doing 3D volume math by hand, plus a bake-time warning when the swap changes batter depth.
- [Building the Brine Calculator: Brining Math Worth Getting Right](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/brine-calculator/): Build notes on the brine calculator: why brining math matters, what it handles — salt type, protein weight, brine strength, time — and how it fits the kit.
- [Building the Universal Recipe Scaler — Local-First, Ad-Free](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/building-the-universal-recipe-scaler/): How I built a free, instant recipe scaler — vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no backend, localStorage, JSON-LD — the regex problem, scale-lock logic, and a clean, fast interface with an interactive prep checklist.
  - The short version: A frustration-driven side project: vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, browser localStorage, no backend, no ads, no signup. Scales ingredient quantities and converts US imperial to metric. The regex problem nobody mentions, the scale-lock logic that ignores temperatures, and a clean, fast interface with an interactive prep checklist.
- [Cook the Way You Want to Cook — Against Culinary Purism](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/cook-the-way-you-want-to-cook/): A daily home cook's argument for cooking the way you want to cook. The only rules worth following are food safety and a few real technique rules. Everything else is yours.
  - The short version: Unless you own a restaurant, cook the way you want to cook. The only rules worth following are food safety and the small set of techniques that are actually physical laws (you can't make a roux without flour and fat). Everything else is opinion.
- [How to Calculate Cost Per Serving (Formula + Examples)](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/cost-per-serving-calculator/): The cost per serving formula with worked examples: package price to per-serving math, waste allowances, and the mistakes that throw the number off.
  - The short version: The cost per serving of a dish is its total ingredient cost — the cost of the amounts you actually used, plus a small waste allowance — divided by the number of servings. The fiddly part is converting package prices into the cost of the portion you actually used, and the one rule that quietly breaks the math is comparing a weight against a volume. This guide walks the whole method by hand, step by step, so the number means something — the free Cost Per Serving Calculator just automates it once you understand it.
- [Dough Hydration Calculator — Baker's Percentages](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/dough-hydration-calculator/): Free baker's-percentage calculator for bread, pizza, pasta, and noodle dough — flour absorbency warnings, egg conversion for fresh pasta, kansui math for ramen.
  - The short version: A free baker's-percentage calculator for bread, pizza, pasta, and noodle doughs. Flour is locked at 100% and everything else scales as a percentage of that flour weight, with two calculation modes (target total dough weight or target flour mass), eleven flour types across five flour groups, six traditional style presets (Neapolitan, sourdough, baguette, ciabatta, Tokyo ramen, soba), and built-in checks for flour absorbency limits, unleavened noodle doughs, kansui salts for ramen, and whole-egg conversions for fresh pasta.
- [How I Actually Cook Rice — The Finger Method, No Measuring Cup](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/how-i-cook-rice-finger-method/): The Vietnamese finger method for rice-cooker water, from someone who has cooked rice a few thousand times. Jasmine rice, rice cooker, no measuring cup required.
  - The short version: Jasmine rice in a rice cooker, rinsed until the water mostly clears, water added by knuckle — small batch uses pinky, larger batch uses index finger. Twenty-five years of finger-measured rice and zero failures I couldn't blame on my own distraction.
- [How I Learned to Cook — From Watching My Dad to Tuesday Gỏi Cuốn](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/how-i-learned-to-cook/): Watching my dad cook most nights, the first dish I made alone at twelve, and why I still cook gỏi cuốn on weeknights — on learning to cook by absorbing it.
  - The short version: On growing up in a Vietnamese-American kitchen, the first thing I cooked alone, why I make gỏi cuốn on weeknights and phở when it matters — and the recipe scaler I built for everyone who learned cooking a different way.
- [How I Make Phở at Home — The Two-Day Method (and Spinach)](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/how-i-make-pho-two-day-method/): A home cook's two-day, stock-first phở bò — every step explained, honest non-traditional choices included (spinach in the bowl), plus a one-day shortcut.
  - The short version: A two-day phở bò method: roast a shin bone, beef knuckle, and oxtail instead of par-boiling (saving the rendered fat as beef tallow), build a rich beef broth on day one for eight hours, and store the bones overnight. On day two, pull those stored bones back out and simmer them in the day-one broth for about five hours, with a spice sachet in the last couple of hours. Use roughly two tablespoons of fish sauce while it cooks — keep it light in the pot and adjust to taste in the bowl. Sautéed garlicky spinach goes at the bottom of the bowl. Squid brand fish sauce. A one-day version is included for when two isn't possible.
- [Most of Cooking Happens at the Cutting Board (My Knife & Board Habits)](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/knife-and-cutting-board-habits/): The Dalstrong Barbarian knives and end-grain Lionswood teak board I bought years before starting the channel, plus the three prep habits that keep them sharp.
  - The short version: Most of scratch cooking happens at the cutting board. Three Dalstrong Barbarian Series knives on a heavy end-grain Lionswood teak board — paired with quick honing before prep, using your knuckle as a guide fence, and two minutes of board oil once a month — keep everything working.
- [Meat Thawing Planner — Real Thermodynamics, Free Tool](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/meat-thawing-planner/): A free calculator for safe meat thawing using real protein-specific thermal math. Refrigerator and cold-water methods, USDA-compliant, with built-in food safety guardrails.
  - The short version: Thawing is where a holiday meal can go wrong before you ever turn the oven on. This is a free, ad-free, local-first utility: pick the protein, the weight, and the method, and it returns a USDA-compliant timeline using protein-specific thawing rates — plus built-in food safety checks, including a 6-hour danger-zone limit for cold-water thawing over 12 lbs, a warning about vacuum-sealed seafood and Clostridium botulinum, and a drip-pan reminder to contain raw runoff in the fridge.
- [Perfect Roast Pull Temp Calculator — Free Carryover Cooking Tool](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/perfect-roast-pull-temp-calculator/): Free carryover cooking calculator: the exact pull-from-heat temp for brisket, duck breast, venison, fish, and steak — resting handled. No signup, no ads.
  - The short version: Most overcooked roasts didn't go wrong in the oven — they kept climbing on the cutting board because of carryover heat. This is a free, ad-free, local-first utility: pick the meat, cut size, and doneness you want, and it returns the exact temperature to pull it from the heat — with dedicated carryover logic for brisket, duck breast, venison, and delicate fish.
- [Reverse Roasting Timeline Calculator — Free Tool](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/reverse-roasting-timeline-calculator/): Free calculator that tells you exactly when to start cooking based on your target dinner time — turkey, prime rib, pork shoulder, salmon, and more. No signup, no ads.
  - The short version: The second free, local-first cooking utility: you enter the protein, weight, and target dinner time, and it outputs the entire backward schedule — preheat, in, out, rest, serve. The honest part of this post is why modeling cooking time accurately is five separate engineering problems, not one multiplication.
- [What I Actually Keep in My Kitchen — A Seven-Ingredient Cooking System](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/what-i-actually-keep-in-my-kitchen/): The pantry list and broth-based weekly system that lets me cook from scratch every night. Plus the honest tired-night meals: fried bologna and scrambled eggs.
  - The short version: Seven ingredients I always have, a Sunday batch of homemade chicken broth that powers five different dinners through the week, and the honest tired-night fallbacks (fried bologna, scrambled eggs) that fill the gap when even the system isn't enough.
- [Why More Home Cooks Should Batch Broths — A Real Cost & Time Breakdown](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/why-home-cooks-should-batch-broths/): Why batching broth weekly pays off for a home cook: real cost and time numbers, plus the techniques that make it work — fat removal, double-strain, demi-glace.
  - The short version: Homemade chicken broth is cheaper than the cheapest boxed broth and tastes better than the most expensive. Roast the bones rather than par-boiling, double-strain, fridge-skim the fat, and reduce a quart into demi-glace cubes for the freezer. One Sunday batch reshapes a week of cooking.
- [Why I Skip Non-Stick (Even Ceramic) — And What’s Actually on My Stove](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/why-i-skip-nonstick-cookware/): Why I skip Teflon and ceramic non-stick pans under high heat, and why bare clad stainless steel and an enameled Dutch oven handle everything on my stove.
  - The short version: I skip Teflon and ceramic non-stick pans because coatings wear down under high heat and heavy daily use. Bare clad stainless steel handles searing, fond, and deglazing, and an enameled cast iron Dutch oven handles soups, braises, and homemade stocks.
- [How to Convert Between Active Dry, Instant, and Fresh Yeast](https://cooking.builtbyjoshstudio.com/blog/yeast-converter/): How to swap one yeast for another — the ratios, why active dry, instant, and fresh aren't interchangeable gram-for-gram, and how the swap affects your rise.
  - The short version: Active dry, instant, and fresh yeast are the same organism carrying different amounts of water, so they aren't interchangeable gram-for-gram — instant is the most concentrated, fresh the least. This guide gives the by-weight conversion ratios in both directions, the packet number worth memorizing (7 g ≈ 2¼ tsp of dry yeast), and why you watch the dough rather than the clock after a swap. The free Yeast Converter does the arithmetic; the fundamentals here tell you what it's doing.
